description: Retrofit the CAM_ISSUE_RESULT machine handback line onto cam issue --file-local and regression-lock cam issue list as deliberately machine-line-free (CAM-197 Layer-1 deterministic-CLI consistency).

userStories.title: Emit CAM_ISSUE_RESULT machine line on cam issue --file-local (all outcomes)
userStories.description: As the orchestrator agent (and any machine consumer of the deterministic CLI), I need cam issue --file-local to emit a parseable CAM_ISSUE_RESULT line on every outcome, mirroring the close/abandon convention from CAM-210, so that the deterministic cam issue surface hands back one consistent machine contract instead of a human printHint plus exit code only.
acceptanceCriteria: cam issue --file-local on success writes BOTH the pre-existing 'filed <id> on main (<sha>)' printHint AND a 'CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id>' line to stdout, and returns exit 0. [oracle: bun test test/issue-dispatch.test.ts]

When createLocalIssueOnMain returns { ok: false, reason }, the command writes 'CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=<reason>' to stdout (reason one of diverged|detached-head|missing-main|guardrail-failed) and returns exit 1; the pre-existing printError fired inside createLocalIssueOnMain is left intact (machine line is additive, not a replacement). [oracle: bun test test/issue-dispatch.test.ts]

With unparseable JSON on stdin, the command writes 'CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=invalid-json' to stdout and returns exit 1; this token is emitted BEFORE createLocalIssueOnMain runs and the pre-existing printError is preserved. [oracle: bun test test/issue-dispatch.test.ts]

When the create path throws (catch block), the command writes 'CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=exception' to stdout and returns exit 1; the pre-existing printError is preserved. [oracle: bun test test/issue-dispatch.test.ts]

The machine line is written via process.stdout.write (never printHint/printError), exactly like close/abandon at index.ts:1489/1493/1502/1506. [oracle: grep -q 'CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=invalid-json' index.ts && grep -q 'CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=exception' index.ts]

Unit tests assert the exact CAM_ISSUE_RESULT line and exit code for each --file-local outcome via injected fakes: the success id line, each of the four createLocalIssueOnMain union reasons (diverged, detached-head, missing-main, guardrail-failed), invalid-json, and exception. [oracle: bun test test/issue-dispatch.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes, including biome lint --error-on-warnings. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: index.ts (dispatchIssue file-local branch, ~lines 1509-1552; convention template at 1489/1493/1502/1506), test/issue-dispatch.test.ts (close/abandon tests at ~494-682 are the shape to mirror, including how they capture stdout). Gotchas from the issue spec: (1) the current result.ok===false path does NOT read result.reason (comment says printError already fired inside createLocalIssueOnMain); the retrofit must now read result.reason for the machine line while leaving that printError intact. (2) invalid-json is a persist-specific token emitted before createLocalIssueOnMain runs (mirrors the CAM-213 cam spec --persist convention); it is NOT a member of the CreateLocalIssueOnMainOutcome union (src/commands/issue-file.ts:86-91). (3) CAM-210 convention: the machine line and exit-code mapping run in dispatchIssue itself regardless of injection; the existing whole-branch fileLocalFn injectable bypasses that printing, so per-outcome tests likely need finer seams mirroring closeIssueOnMainFn (e.g. an injectable createLocalIssueOnMainFn plus a stdin-text seam on IssueDispatchDeps); keep the existing fileLocalFn injectable working so current branch-isolation tests stay green (discriminated-union parseXxxArgs + injectable-deps pattern in scripts/cam/patterns.md). (4) Out of scope: createLocalIssueOnMain internals, new CLI flags, close/abandon (done in CAM-210). Do NOT edit .claude/commands/cam-issue.md or templates/ (the slash-command output contract already ends with CAM_ISSUE_RESULT and the CLI line is additive; touching templates would drag in vendor re-embed, out of scope here). noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on repo-wide: guard any array/regex-group access touched.

userStories.title: Regression-lock cam issue list as CAM_ISSUE_RESULT-free by design
userStories.description: As a future reviewer or maintainer, I need the deliberate absence of a CAM_ISSUE_RESULT line on cam issue list encoded as an explicit regression test and an in-code design note, so that list's handback (rendered table plus process exit code) is recognized as a mutation-outcome-contract decision and never flagged or 'fixed' as an omission.
acceptanceCriteria: cam issue list emits NO CAM_ISSUE_RESULT line on any code path; its output remains the rendered table and the process exit code is the sole machine signal. [oracle: bun test]
A regression test asserts that the list dispatch path writes no CAM_ISSUE_RESULT substring to stdout. [oracle: bun test test/issue-dispatch.test.ts]
runIssueList and the list branch of dispatchIssue contain no CAM_ISSUE_RESULT emission. [oracle: ! grep -q 'CAM_ISSUE_RESULT' src/commands/issue-list.ts]

The list branch of dispatchIssue carries a short comment documenting the deliberate decision: CAM_ISSUE_RESULT is a mutation-outcome contract (the id of the single acted-on issue, or ERROR) and list is a read over many issues with no id. [oracle: grep -qi 'mutation-outcome' index.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes, including biome lint --error-on-warnings. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: index.ts (dispatchIssue list branch, ~lines 1478-1482: comment only, no behavior change), test/issue-dispatch.test.ts (regression test; capture stdout the same way the US-001 tests do and assert the captured output contains no CAM_ISSUE_RESULT substring when mode==='list' dispatches). runIssueList internals (src/commands/issue-list.ts) are out of scope: read-only verification via the negative grep, no edits there. This story is deliberately behavior-neutral: it exists to encode the design decision from the CAM-212 spec (gotcha: 'the list no-line outcome is a deliberate design decision, not a forgotten path') so a future reviewer does not retrofit a speculative machine token onto list. Do not invent any new machine line or flag for list.
